findings.claim: Raw meat, fish and poultry must be stored on the bottom shelf to prevent drip contamination of ready-to-eat foods stored below.
findings.truth: Bottom-shelf storage prevents raw juices dripping onto other foods; there are no foods stored below the bottom shelf.
findings.evidence: Food Standards Agency food-storage guidance; specification 2.1 Food spoilage, cross-contamination

findings.claim: The spec lists ten functional / chemical properties across four ingredient categories.
findings.truth: The specification names twelve items: 2 carbohydrate, 4 fat/oil, 4 protein, and 2 fruit/vegetable working, functional or chemical properties.
findings.evidence: specification 2.1 The science of food, functional and chemical properties list

findings.claim: All B vitamins are water-soluble and therefore cannot be stored in the body.
findings.truth: Vitamin B12 is water-soluble but body stores can last around 2 to 5 years. It is an exception to this generalisation.
findings.evidence: NHS, Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia: Causes

findings.claim: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia.
findings.truth: Pernicious anaemia is an autoimmune cause of vitamin B12 deficiency. Deficiency can cause megaloblastic anaemia and neurological damage.
findings.evidence: NHS, Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia: Causes

findings.claim: Six life stages, including primary-aged children, are examined.
findings.truth: The specification names five life-stage categories: toddlers, teenagers, early adulthood, middle adulthood and late adulthood. It does not name primary-aged children as a category.
findings.evidence: specification 2.1 Principles of nutrition, Diet and good health

findings.claim: All 11–18-year-olds need 1,000 mg of calcium per day.
findings.truth: The UK calcium RNI is 1,000 mg/day for boys aged 11–18 and 800 mg/day for girls aged 11–18; the adult RNI is 700 mg/day.

findings.claim: Vitamin D supplementation is recommended for all adults over 65.
findings.truth: UK advice is that everyone should consider 10 µg of vitamin D daily in autumn and winter. A year-round supplement is advised for people with little or no sunlight exposure; age over 65 alone is not the stated criterion.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, vitamin D guidance for vulnerable groups

findings.claim: Breast milk iron stores from birth deplete around six months.
findings.truth: Healthy term infants are born with iron stores accumulated in utero. Together with iron in breast milk, these meet needs for about the first six months.
findings.evidence: SACN Feeding in the First Year of Life report

findings.claim: A low-fat label means a product was reformulated to reduce fat compared with the standard version.
findings.truth: A low-fat claim is a legal threshold: no more than 3 g fat per 100 g for solids or 1.5 g per 100 ml for liquids. It is not a comparison with a standard version.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Nutrition and health claims made on foods

findings.claim: Cast iron is one of the best heat conductors in a kitchen and heats evenly.
findings.truth: Cast iron retains heat well but conducts heat less well than copper and aluminium, so it is not an especially even heat conductor.
findings.evidence: GE Appliances cookware guide; UCSB Science Line heat-transfer explanation

findings.claim: The specification identifies ten functional properties across carbohydrates, fats, proteins, fruit and vegetables.
findings.truth: The specification names twelve working, functional and chemical properties across those four ingredient categories.
findings.evidence: specification 2.1 The science of food, functional and chemical properties list

findings.claim: Carbohydrate energy must be taught as 3.75 kcal per gram, while another lesson teaches 4 kcal per gram.
findings.truth: Use 3.75 kcal/g when calculating dietary energy with the current SACN convention, or 4 kcal/g when calculating declared food-label energy under retained food-information law. The specification does not select one. Recommendation: state the convention in both lessons and use it consistently.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK SACN statement on energy factors; Retained Regulation (EU) 1169/2011, Annex XIV

findings.claim: This topic will typically have a 12-mark Evaluate question.
findings.truth: The specification sets a 100-mark written paper with two compulsory sections but does not prescribe a 12-mark Evaluate question by topic. An official 2023 review shows a 12-mark question existed, without confirming this command word or topic. Recommendation: verify against the accessible official paper or recast this as house practice guidance.
findings.evidence: specification Summary of assessment and written-assessment section; WJEC 2023 Online Exam Review

summary: Nine lessons checked. Eleven verified factual or scope corrections are supplied; two assessment or convention issues require editorial judgement rather than an automated edit.
